ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Constitution of the Republic of South Africa, 1996; Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022, s 56 (beneficial ownership records); Companies Regulations, 2011 (GNR 351 of 26 April 2011), reg 15 (name reservation); Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001, as amended by the Financial Intelligence Centre Amendment Act 1 of 2017, ss 1, 20A-20E, 21C-21I and 37 (UBO and PEP duties of accountable institutions); Protection of Constitutional Democracy Against Terrorism and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004, s 12; CIPC Beneficial Ownership Filing Practice Note (2023); FIC Directive 6 (2023) on Beneficial Ownership.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified notarial copy of passport or national identity document of each director, shareholder and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or civil registry of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement) of each director, shareholder and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or regulated financial institution of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and board resolution of any foreign corporate shareholder authorizing the incorporation of the South African subsidiary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry and notary public of the foreign jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and UBOs against the UN financial sanctions lists, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated List, and domestic FIC financial sanctions lists at onboarding and on an ongoing basis. PEP identification and enhanced due diligence are mandatory for domestic and foreign prominent public officials, their family members and close associates under FICA Part 6 and FIC Guidance Note 7. Because the target payment rails (AdMob and AppLovin) settle in US dollars, OFAC compliance is a practical prerequisite for bank account opening and payment processing. Delistings, negative news checks and politically exposed person screening must be documented in the pre-incorporation due diligence file and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) eServices / BizPortal — www.cipc.co.za
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name may be in any of the 11 official South African languages but must be rendered in Latin script; CIPC digital filing accepts standard Latin-alphabet characters only and diacritics are typically normalized. The statutory suffix '(Pty) Ltd' (or '(Proprietary) Limited') is mandatory for a private company under s 11(1) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008. The registered name must be identical to the reserved name, and a distinct 'distinguishing element' is required where the core name resembles an existing mark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation approved under Form CoR 9.1 is valid for 180 days and may be extended once for a further 180 days by filing an extension application with CIPC before expiry. Upon rejection under s 16(4) (confusingly similar, offensive, or prohibited token), the applicant may within 20 business days file an application with the Companies Tribunal under s 160 using Form CTR 142, seeking an order directing CIPC to reconsider the reservation. Practical SOP: (i) review the CIPC refusal rationale and re-run the CIPC search database; (ii) amend the proposed name by adding a distinctive token or a different primary element; (iii) re-file CoR 9.1 with the revised name; (iv) escalate to the Companies Tribunal only where the name is commercially essential.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for CIPC registration and annual return purposes provided the registered office is a physical South African street address at which service of process can be effected during business hours (s 23 of the Companies Act; a post box is prohibited). A serviced-office virtual address is the prevailing market norm for a hyper-casual gaming publisher. To strengthen commercial substance, support tax residence and reduce SARS audit risk, a leased desk or co-working presence plus a local director or company secretary is recommended; a purely address-only arrangement without any local activity is commercially feasible but carries elevated substance-review risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 5-10% per annum) for a standard low-risk private gaming publisher with a compliant registered office and a complete beneficial ownership filing. CIPC Inspection and Enforcement may conduct unannounced onsite inspections under ss 178-183 of the Companies Act following complaints or risk flags, and SARS or the FIC may conduct audits or visits. Probability rises to approximately 25% per annum where only a virtual or serviced address is maintained without any physical local footprint, or where beneficial ownership filings are delayed or incomplete.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024; ss 11-12 (company names), s 13 (incorporation), s 14 (registration), s 19 (effect of registration), s 23 (registered office), ss 66-70 (first directors), ss 76-77 (directors' duties); Companies Regulations, 2011, Reg 14 (Notice of Incorporation).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic), Republic of South Africa.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with an executed Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI); the CIPC issues the Registration Certificate (Form CoR 14.3) as conclusive evidence of incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum issued or paid-up share capital applies to a (Pty) Ltd under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; the MOI may authorise a nominal capital. Shares may be issued for cash or in-kind consideration, and no escrow or trust-account deposit is mandated for incorporation of a private company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED as the first board resolution of the Company: (1) the incorporation effected under the Companies Act 71 of 2008 is ratified; (2) the share subscriptions offered in the Memorandum of Incorporation are accepted, the authorised shares are allotted and issued to the subscribing shareholders, and consideration is satisfied as recorded; (3) the registered office of the Company is established at the physical address in the Notice of Incorporation within the Republic of South Africa; (4) the persons identified in the consent notices are appointed as directors and officers with powers delegated under the MOI; and (5) the directors and officers are authorised to open banking accounts and conclude all ancillary documents, filings and agreements to give effect to this incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services portal, Company Name Reservation module (www.cipc.co.za / CorpBiz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the CIPC transactional e-services portal, initiate the 'Reserve a Name' application (Form CoR 9.1), and submit the proposed name 'ZA PTY LTD' (or a structurally equivalent variant) for similarity screening under s 11 of the Companies Act. Pay the R50 reservation fee electronically, and await the reservation certificate; if the name contains 'ZA' and is considered to resemble a governmental identifier, CIPC may require a written consent or explanatory justification under s 11(5).
required_dossiers: Completed Form CoR 9.1 (name reservation application)
Certified copy of the incorporator's identity document or passport
Power of attorney where an agent lodges the application
Payment proof for the reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, lodge a fresh CoR 9.1 listing alternative names, or file a representation to the CIPC Registrar within 20 business days; where consent is requested, submit a supporting affidavit explaining the absence of misleading association.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of MOI and Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporating directors and legal counsel; final lodgement is effected with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation in accordance with the Companies Act 71 of 2008, prescribing the share structure, authorised shares, directorial appointment and removal provisions, and the registered office; execute the MOI by each subscriber or incorporator under s 13. Complete Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation), annex the executed MOI and the written consents to act as first directors, and arrange notarisation or certified signature verification where non-resident subscribers participate.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation)
Written consents to act as first directors (Form CoR 15.1A equivalents)
Certified identity documents and tax reference numbers of incorporators and first directors
Name reservation certificate (where obtained)
Declaration of compliance signed by an attorney or an incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where CIPC queries defects in the MOI, file amendments through the transactional case file and resubmit within the prescribed response period; a legal practitioner may file a supplementary declaration of compliance to cure procedural irregularities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Lodgement, Fee Settlement and Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services 'Company Registration' filing channel (CorpBiz / current CIPC online case filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the complete incorporation package to the CIPC portal, settle the statutory filing fee (ZAR 175, approximately USD 10, plus name-reservation fee where applicable) by debit order or electronic transfer, and submit for statutory vetting. Upon approval, CIPC registers the company and issues the Registration Certificate (Form CoR 14.3), which takes effect on the date of registration and is conclusive evidence of juristic existence under s 19(1).
required_dossiers: Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation)
Executed MOI
Consent to act as directors
Certified identity documents of first directors and incorporators
Proof of payment of filing fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected, rectify the defects identified in the electronic rejection notice and resubmit within 30 days; where the rejection is unlawful, escalate to the CIPC helpdesk, the Companies Tribunal, or the High Court for review under s 26 of the Companies Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convening of the First Board Meeting, Registered Office Adoption and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: In-house First Board of Directors; CIPC for notification of any post-registration changes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting in person or by written resolution, adopt the pro-forma first board resolution set out above, ratify the allotment and issue of shares, adopt the South African physical registered office address required by s 23(3), appoint the executive directors and officers, open a corporate bank account, and instruct the secretary or accounting officer to maintain the statutory registers (securities register and directors' register).
required_dossiers: Minutes or written resolution of the first board meeting
Share subscription schedules and allotment records
Proof of the registered office address (lease or letter of consent)
Appointment letters and consent forms for officers
Bank account opening application and board mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any omission in share allotment or officer appointment is ratified by a supplemental board resolution; if ratification is impossible, an application may be made to the Companies Tribunal or the High Court for a declaratory order under ss 20 and 26.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax and Supplementary Statutory Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); CIPC beneficial-ownership filing; Department of Employment and Labour (COIDA/UIF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax and, where applicable, VAT and PAYE through SARS eFiling or a SARS branch within 21 days of incorporation; register with the Department of Employment and Labour for UIF and COIDA if employees are engaged; file the beneficial-ownership schedule with CIPC in accordance with s 56 of the Companies Act; and appoint a POPIA information officer where personal data is processed in game publishing.
required_dossiers: Registration Certificate (Form CoR 14.3)
MOI and first board resolution
Director identity documents and tax numbers
SARS company registration form and supporting proof of address
Beneficial-ownership declaration schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS or CIPC rejects a submission, remedy the noted non-compliance and resubmit corrected filings; apply for remission of administrative penalties under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 (ss 214 and 227(e)) and lodge internal appeal objections within 30 days of notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the publishing of lightweight ad-monetised mobile games (ISIC 5820) does not constitute an industrial activity subject to a licensing board; the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic) retains general oversight for consumer protection, advertising standards and the classification of game content.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating or manufacturing permit is required for a South African hyper-casual games publisher whose services are digital, server-hosted and non-physical; the company may operate under its CIPC Registration Certificate and SARS tax registration alone.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE), successor to the Department of Environmental Affairs
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no listed activity under the EIA Regulations, 2014 (GNR 982) is triggered by office-based software publishing with zero physical manufacturing, zero land disturbance and zero effluent generation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No discharge, VOC, wastewater or hazardous-waste thresholds apply to server-hosted digital publishing; if office hardware or e-waste is generated, disposal must comply with the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008 and municipal WEEE collection rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 compliance applies to the leased registered office: fire-safety equipment certification, electrical certificate of compliance and a certificate of occupancy from the local municipality; structural load inspections are not applicable to a non-industrial office environment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); eFiling portal at www.sars.gov.za
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must register for income tax and, where applicable, VAT by submitting a completed SARS registration form (e.g., VAT101, IT registration via eFiling) accompanied by constitutive documents, alien/foreign director identification, and SARS Corporate Income Tax registration confirmation. A South African tax reference number (TIN) and separate VAT vendor number are issued. Non-resident companies with a representative office or Permanent Establishment in South Africa require registration; foreign-owned resident companies are normally registered upon incorporation through CIPC linkage.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under South African law. A (Pty) Ltd is automatically a resident tax company if incorporated in South Africa. Election mechanisms are limited to special tax regimes (e.g., deemed CFC election, hedging/valuation elections, and s11E allowances); hybrid mismatch rules in s23M of the Income Tax Act apply and no elective hybrid classification is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax under the South African Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration: ZAR 1,000,000 of taxable supplies in the preceding 12 months or reasonable expectation of exceeding ZAR 1,000,000 in the next 12 months; voluntary registration: ZAR 50,000 of taxable supplies in the preceding 12 months.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or continuous transaction control (CTC) mandate applies. SARS eFiling is the mandatory electronic tax return channel, and suppliers must issue full tax invoices containing the VAT vendor registration number, invoice date, description, consideration, and VAT amount (VAT Act s20). Digital stamping and government-authorised e-invoicing clearance are not currently required; however, SARS may require electronic submission of VAT201 returns and supporting schedules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under s11(1) of the VAT Act. Goods are zero-rated when the supplier exports the goods in the ordinary course of business under customs supervision. Services are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident who is not in South Africa at the time, provided the services are not directly connected to movable or immovable property in South Africa, and the supplier retains documentary proof of non-resident status. For hyper-casual mobile games, ad revenue and app-store receipts from foreign platforms may qualify as exported services where the recipient is a non-resident and the services are consumed outside South Africa, subject to a permissible invoice and proof-of-export record.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500/SAD500J) lodged via SARS Customs
Bill of Lading or Airwaybill evidencing physical export of goods
Inward Remittance Certificate from a South African Authorised Dealer proving foreign currency receipt
Commercial invoice and, where applicable, non-resident declaration or legalized proof of foreign residency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may verify export zero-rating through audits and risk assessments. Incorrect or fraudulent zero-rating triggers a VAT understatement penalty under the Tax Administration Act of up to 150% of the tax shortfall, statutory interest, and potential criminal prosecution (VAT Act s73, Tax Administration Act s234). Retrospective clawbacks can apply for up to five years from the date of assessment, with extended periods in cases of deliberate tax evasion or non-disclosure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) - Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), acting jointly with the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) as the AML/CFT supervisor under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA). Authorised Dealers (commercial banks with exchange-control licences) administer day-to-day foreign-exchange transactions on behalf of SARB.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa operates a partially liberalised exchange-control regime under the Currency and Exchanges Manual (CEM), with the rand (ZAR) as a managed-float, non-internationalised currency. Current-account transactions are fully convertible without prior SARB approval: export proceeds from software and gaming services, royalties, advertising payouts and management fees may be repatriated through any Authorised Dealer subject to documentary verification, purpose-code declaration and balance-of-payments reporting. Capital-account transactions remain subject to administered liberalisation: inbound equity investment is freely permitted but must be routed through an Authorised Dealer and formally registered as imported capital (share-subscription declaration) so that subsequent profit repatriation is recognised. Profit remittance of dividends is permissible without FinSurv approval if the paying company has a valid SARS tax-clearance status, the underlying capital inflow was registered with the AD, non-resident dividend withholding tax (statutory 15%, possibly reduced under an applicable tax treaty) is deducted and declared, and the bank's foreign dividend reporting forms are completed. Practical hurdles include the obligation to prove the provenance of every inbound capital credit, matching purpose codes to the bank's nature-of-transaction list, and the ban on speculative or uncovered ZAR hedging, which limits treasury flexibility for early-stage hyper-casual operators.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For exported services (hyper-casual game publishing and programmatic in-game advertising), the full value of export proceeds must be received through an Authorised Dealer in South Africa within 180 days of the invoice date or the date on which the service is rendered. There is no mandatory percentage conversion ratio into ZAR in the current dispensation; surrender is satisfied by crediting the proceeds to the exporting entity's Foreign Currency Account (FCA) held with a domestic AD, where USD may be retained indefinitely or converted at the prevailing managed-float rate. Quarterly or event-driven exchange-control reporting requires the inward SWIFT credits to match the declared SARB purpose code for software/IT services, backed by Google AdMob/AppLovin payout statements, signed publisher agreements, and reconciliation of the ad-network settlement cycle. Export proceeds not received within 180 days require a formal extension application to FinSurv; non-compliance is an exchange-control contravention carrying administrative penalties and potential criminal sanctions under the Exchange Control Regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.trade_related_purpose_code_framework: Inbound and outbound wire transfers must be annotated with SARB-recognised purpose codes reflecting the nature of the transaction. The hyper-casual gaming revenue stream is generally classified under the current-account software-services or electronic-commerce category, while the original share subscription by the non-resident parent is classified as a capital-account direct-investment inflow. The Authorised Dealer captures these codes in the daily BOP reporting and reconciles each MT103 credit to the underlying AdMob/AppLovin settlement statement; misclassification of revenue as capital or vice versa triggers automatic compliance holds and potential reclassification penalties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational ZAR Business Account + USD Foreign Currency Account (FCA); capital-escrow sleeve available for imported-capital registration
Operational Business Account + USD/EUR FCA; eFICA remote onboarding and integrated treasury platform
Operational Business Account + FCA; corporate FX desk with dedicated capital-subscription registration support
Operational Corporate Account + FCA; trade and clearing rails for MT103 and documentary credits
Operational Corporate Cash Manager Account + FCA; treasury and FX hedging focus

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of China Johannesburg Branch (formerly Mercantile Bank Limited)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account + USD FCA; trade-finance niche for China-corridor ad-tech vendors

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Offshore digital EMI rails (Wise Business, Payoneer, DLocal, Airwallex, MultiPass) are legally usable as collection wallets for hyper-casual advertising revenue but cannot replace a domestic Authorised Dealer relationship. A South African (Pty) Ltd may receive USD from Google AdMob/AppLovin into an EMI USD wallet and thereafter repatriate to a local AD-held FCA, provided the EMI acts only as a collection conduit and each repatriation is supported by purpose-code declarations, payout statements and publisher contracts. However, Wise South Africa and similar providers are accountable institutions under the FIC Act, not banks; they cannot provide onshore ZAR settlement or exchange-control surrender. Retaining export proceeds with a non-AD intermediary beyond short settlement windows creates an unrepatriated-export-proceeds red flag, and domestic banks will demand full SWIFT/beneficiary statements before accepting drawdowns from an EMI. The recommended architecture is direct settlement from ad networks to a tier-1 AD FCA; EMIs should be reserved for small-value high-frequency payouts below USD 10,000 per day or for ad networks that cannot wire to a South African FCA.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under FICA, as amended by the FIC Amendment Act 2022, South African banks apply risk-based customer due diligence. For a low-risk standard customer such as ZA_PTY_LTD, at least one authorised director or natural-person beneficial owner holding more than 25% of the entity must complete an identity verification process that includes a live interview, conducted either in-branch or through a sanctioned remote-video verification system operated by the bank's eFICA platform. Fully remote account opening is available at Standard Bank, FNB, Absa and Nedbank where the director is a low-risk foreign tax resident, with certified copies of CIPC registration, Memorandum of Incorporation and beneficial-ownership register to be produced through a South African attorney or notary within 60 days. Foreign-resident directors must supply apostilled or notarially certified passports, proof of residential address and a tax-residency certificate; at least one physical or video interview with each significant beneficial owner is mandated before transactional limits are elevated above the basic threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder with opaque ultimate beneficial ownership, such as an offshore holding company in BVI, Hong Kong or Cyprus holding more than 25% of the (Pty) Ltd, triggering the mandatory beneficial-ownership uplift rule.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC beneficial-ownership register; organisational chart and share-register trail; notarised board resolution of the foreign parent identifying all natural-person beneficial owners; apostilled passports; source-of-wealth affidavit; CRS/FATCA self-certification forms; licensed third-party background screening report for each beneficial owner; letter from the corporate-services provider confirming the ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity, low-ticket microtransactions from programmatic advertising (Google AdMob/AppLovin) generating thousands of daily credits that the bank's transaction-monitoring engine flags as unusual velocity or potential layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed AdMob/AppLovin publisher agreements; monthly payout reconciliation statements from both networks; dashboard screenshots of settlement cycles; explanation of unit economics (eCPI/eCPM and advertiser-to-network-to-publisher flow); business-model narrative letter; completed bank source-of-funds questionnaire; contractual chain-of-funds diagram; do-not-resolve letter expressly acknowledging the ad-tech flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection sourced from cryptocurrency liquidation by the foreign shareholder; FICA's updated guidance treats crypto-asset exposures as a heightened money-laundering risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete crypto-exchange transaction reports including buy-to-wallet and wallet-to-bank off-ramp trail; blockchain-analytics report from a recognised provider; executed settlement letters from the exchange; proof of off-ramp to a regulated bank account in the shareholder's jurisdiction; sworn affidavit of source of wealth; if the proceeds pass through an intermediary, the deed of donation or loan agreement and full KYC pack on the intermediary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated entity with no 12-month operating history or unaudited financials, raising concerns about lawful business substance and the durability of the revenue model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC company profile and registered address; opening balance sheet certified by a South African accountant; notarised declaration of intended business activities; 24-month cash-flow forecast linked to signed ad-network contracts; executed revenue contracts with Google AdMob and AppLovin; office lease and operational-substance evidence; SARS registration and tax-compliance status (TAXSTAT); reference letter from the incorporating law firm or home-country bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP hits, or name mismatches, involving advertising-technology counterparties, traffic brokers or the beneficiaries of outbound trade disbursements (traffic arbitrage, bot traffic or non-contracted intermediaries).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC, EU, UN and South African targeted-financial-sanctions screening reports for every counterparty; trailing documentation for each inbound MT103 including payment reference and publisher statement; risk-tiering memorandum classifying AdMob and AppLovin as low-risk supervised institutions; contractual sanctions-exclusion and anti-fraud warranties in all publisher agreements; KYC packs on subcontractors receiving outbound disbursements; internal AML policy manual of the (Pty) Ltd.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident parent transfers USD/EUR by SWIFT MT103 to the (Pty) Ltd's domestic Foreign Currency Account using the Authorised Dealer's capital-account purpose code for direct investment or equity subscription. The AD requires: (a) a board resolution of the company accepting the subscription and issuing ordinary shares; (b) the CIPC allotment and beneficial-ownership filing; (c) a signed share-purchase declaration whereby the AD registers the funds as imported capital, thereby enabling future dividend and capital repatriation without further FinSurv approval; (d) for intercompany loans, a formal loan agreement and transfer-pricing/interest-rate file satisfying the thin-capitalisation limitation under section 23N of the Income Tax Act. Every inbound credit must carry the remitter reference and be reconciled to the bank's balance-of-payments reporting within the prescribed settlement window. Where the parent funds the company through an EMI (Payoneer/Wise), the domestic AD will treat the EMI as a mere collection agent and will require the full underlying transaction chain before releasing balances for operational withdrawal.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements to SDK providers, app-store accounts, ad-tech vendors, traffic suppliers and intellectual-property licensors are executed through: (i) SWIFT MT103 direct corporate transfers, each linked to an underlying invoice and accompanied by the appropriate current-account purpose code and, where applicable, SARS tax clearance and withholding-tax calculation on royalties; (ii) MT202/MT203 for bank-to-bank positioning between the FCA and the ZAR settlement account; (iii) commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700) where the supplier requires documentary security for high-value licences or bulk advertising inventory; and (iv) the domestic real-time clearing rails (SAMOS/RBPS) for ZAR payments to South African counterparties. All outward disbursements from non-resident proceeds are subject to the bank's FX compliance checklist, which includes proof of the underlying service, transfer-pricing documentation for intercompany technology or marketing fees, and verification that the beneficiary is not on any sanctions list or subject to enhanced due-diligence holds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable ZAR/USD forward exchange contract (FEC) with a domestic Authorised Dealer, limited to hedges of confirmed AdMob/AppLovin receivables and other current-account exposures, with a maximum tenor of 12 months absent FinSurv approval.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on ZAR, permissible only where FinSurv authorises the specific hedge or the counterparty is a non-resident hedging its own exposure; for an onshore (Pty) Ltd the practical and compliant instrument is the deliverable FEC.

FX option strategies, including zero-cost collars and purchased USD/ZAR put or call options, where the notional does not exceed the underlying contracted future ad-network receipts and where no naked or speculative option writing occurs.

Cross-currency interest-rate swap (CCIRS) linked to an external shareholder loan or US-denominated working capital facility, matching notional, coupon dates and amortisation to the underlying debt service obligation.

FX swap (roll-over) transactions through the AD treasury desk for day-to-day FCA liquidity repositioning and funding of near-term ZAR disbursements, provided each leg is tied to a genuine current-account or registered capital-account exposure.

Natural hedge through retention of USD in the domestic Foreign Currency Account, which avoids realised conversion losses and is treated as a permissible passive treasury position rather than speculative exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary date of incorporation; not financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CIPC late-filing penalty and reinstatement costs after deregistration; failure to submit for two consecutive years is ground for administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC when AFS filing is statutorily required; otherwise board and shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after financial year-end; board approval and signature of directors required before filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Compliance notice from CIPC; directors may incur personal liability for continued non-compliance; criminal penalties apply under Companies Act ss.30, 33.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Declaration (Register of Beneficial Owners confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the CIPC annual return; within 5 business days after any change in beneficial ownership or shareholding
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under the Companies Act and FIC Act; CIPC may issue compliance notices, reject annual return, or impose administrative penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the tax return due date issued by SARS, generally within 12 months after financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Understatement penalty of 10%-200% plus interest; criminal prosecution for intentional failure to file.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Two top-up instalments during the tax year (typically by end of June and end of February/SARS schedule) plus final top-up by the annual ITR14 due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 20% administrative penalty and interest on under-estimates; higher penalty for gross negligence or intentional submission.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A full independent audit is compulsory when Public Interest Score (PIS) exceeds 350. PIS between 100 and 350 requires an independent review, not full audit. PIS below 100 requires neither unless the MOI, shareholders, CIPC, or applicable regulations require it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or IFRS for SMEs (as prescribed by the Companies Act); no general local GAAP. Financial statements must be in ZAR and present fairly the company's financial position.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain an internal register of beneficial owners and confirm it annually through the CIPC annual return. Any share transfer or change in ownership must be recorded in that register and reported to CIPC within 5 business days, supported by the prescribed share transfer instrument and board resolution.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Prescribed Officers
Minute Book of shareholder and board meetings
Statutory accounting records and supporting documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 80-300 per year for CIPC-registered physical office and company secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0 if no statutory audit required (low PIS); ~800-3,500 for independent review; ~5,000-25,000 for full IFRS audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; 28% prior)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Section 11D R&D incentive: 150% deduction for qualifying R&D expenditure approved by the Department of Science and Innovation. Section 12B: 125% first-year allowance on qualifying renewable-energy plant. Small Business Corporation (SBC) schedule: 0%–21% progressive rates on taxable income up to ZAR 550,000 (thereafter 27%) only where all shareholders are natural persons and annual turnover does not exceed ZAR 20 million — unavailable to a entity with corporate shareholders. No patent-box or IP regime for gaming software.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite — no statutory expiry in South Africa (contrary to the default of 5 years in the schema; s20A ITA may deny an assessed loss if a >50% ownership change occurs and the same trade is not continued with profit intention)
